rationale: A heading whose TEXT equals its parent's text published no `contains` edge at all, because both ends of the edge spell the same word and the analyzer's edge builder drops a self-edge. The two sites are genuinely distinct — a child's identity is qualified by its parent, so `## Changelog` under `# Changelog` is `Changelog.Changelog` — but the published contract spelling of a first occurrence is the bare display text, so the strings collided. The differential found it rather than the read, and found it quietly: the tree oracle derives the edge from the grammar, the analyzer did not have it, and the whole kubernetes draw missed by one edge in roughly one draw in nine (`vendor/github.com/google/uuid/CHANGELOG.md`, 1 MISSING out of ~5800 tree-truth edges). A one-in-nine rate with a gate that reports only a count is a rate at which a reader writes the number off as sampling noise, which is why the edge this pins is worth a fixture even though it is one relationship. The repeated-sibling half (`## Example` twice under one parent -> `Example#2`, both children of `Setup`) is in the same fixture because the two rules are easy to confuse: a repeat gets a site suffix, a same-text-as-parent does not, and getting them backwards would publish a hierarchy that looks plausible and is wrong. forbidSymbols pins the contract half — the qualified path is an INTERNAL id and must not surface as a published name, which is what keeps the collision possible in the first place and is why this class could not be fixed by publishing qualified names everywhere.

_seamNote.what: The fix is one boolean at the heading-hierarchy call site, and it is a claim about identity rather than about strings: `ownerId !== id` cannot be false for a non-empty heading name, because a child's id is `${ownerId}.${name}` with an optional `#n` site suffix.
_seamNote.why: Publishing qualified ids everywhere would remove the collision by removing the contract spelling, but the contract spelling is the reader-facing name and changing it would rename every section in every markdown document in the index. The distinction the guard was reaching for — does this edge point at the same node twice? — is a question about identity, and only identity can answer it. The self-edge filter stays for every other call site, where source and target genuinely are the same string because there is only one site involved.
